normative_summary: Each Renderer Command represents exactly one RenderDocument root Canvas.
Each Renderer Command atomically produces one complete image.
Repeat, Conditional, TemplateUse, and compositionViewport only affect content inside that image.
A child viewport never becomes an independent output.
Multiple Templates, inputs, variants, DPIs, or formats are orchestrated outside Engine as independent Commands.
Renderer v1 has no outputs array, page, batch, or partial-success semantics.
Output covers the complete root Canvas physical surface including authored bleed.
Callers cannot request node export, crop, resize, target dimensions, rotation, background override, bleed toggle, or secondary layout.
The single-Canvas and no-multi-Canvas-flow constraints remain authoritative.
RenderEngine is an internal component of the Rendering bounded context.
Public clients may call only the Rendering API and cannot submit or obtain Engine-internal contracts, identities, leases, or controls.
Engine cannot read Template, DesignDSL, RootDocument, caller tokens, or business identity.
The Layout Profile independently freezes measure, arrange, and shaping semantics.
The Renderer Profile independently freezes resource interpretation, color, raster, sampling, code, and pixel algorithms.
The PNG Output Profile independently freezes PNG bytes and metadata.
The JPEG Output Profile independently freezes JPEG bytes and metadata.
The server maintains an immutable exact compatibility table that selects one complete profile combination per allowed public request.
Callers cannot select profiles or request latest, negotiation, or fallback behavior.
A rendered subtree cannot mix profile versions.
One Evaluation may produce multiple output Commands only outside Engine.
Every output Command independently re-enters Engine.
Renderer v1 provides no cross-request RenderOutput cache.
Engine output is transient and does not create files, URLs, Artifacts, Workspace items, revisions, or history.
Formal output and Authoritative Preview use the same Evaluation, compatibility table, and RenderEngine path.
Preview may request an ordinary lower DPI or another allowed format.
Equal effective document, Profile, DPI, and quality inputs must produce identical image bytes regardless of formal-output or preview purpose.
A browser-local canvas is always non-authoritative.
Renderer Command input is strict UTF-8 JSON.
Renderer Command rejects duplicate keys.
Renderer Command rejects unknown members.
Renderer Command rejects null values.
Renderer Command rejects unknown exact Profiles and non-canonical scalars.
The example document object is only a formatting placeholder and cannot validate independently of a complete RenderDocument.
Rendering generates requestId as a canonical lowercase UUID v4.
The Command document is the complete Ticket15 RenderDocument.
Engine verifies renderDocumentDigest with renderweave-render-c14n/1.0 before use.
Rendering expands deadlineAt from server policy as an absolute UTC deadline.
deadlineAt wire form is RFC3339 UTC with exactly three millisecond digits.
Public callers may request at most a duration.
Public callers cannot submit arbitrary absolute deadlines.
A PNG output object contains exactly profile and dpi.
A JPEG output object contains exactly profile, dpi, and quality.
DPI is a positive integer.
An omitted public DPI expands to 96 before Command construction.
JPEG quality is an integer from 1 through 100.
An omitted JPEG quality expands to 90 before Command construction.
The output object has no redundant format member because profile uniquely determines the format and encoding contract.
The exact Command canonical profile is renderweave-render-command-c14n/1.0.
Command canonicalization reuses Render member ordering and escaping rules.
Command canonicalization uses shortest integer form and rejects unknown or null members.
Semantic arrays retain their defined order during Command canonicalization.
The canonical writer never repairs invalid input.
rendererCommandDigest uses the specified domain-separated SHA-256 formula over canonical effective Command bytes.
rendererCommandDigest is used only for Engine registry identity, resend conflict detection, and cancel.
rendererCommandDigest is excluded from Command, image bytes, public response, logs, Template or Evaluation identity, Artifact identity, and cross-request caches.
The public API exposes only PNG or JPEG, DPI, and JPEG quality.
Rendering expands public parameters through an immutable exact-profile and default mapping.
An existing supported public mapping cannot silently change its output algorithm.
A mapping or observable-output change requires a new API and Profile combination.
Command HTTP entities use application/vnd.renderweave.render-command+json with version 1.0.
The embedded contractVersion remains wire authority and cannot be replaced or relaxed by a media parameter.
The Engine channel uses encryption and authenticated workload identity.
Authentication failure is rejected before JSON parsing.
Command carries no user credential, bearer token, or permission declaration.
Command, cancel, and resend for one requestId route to one linearizable registry shard.
The first legal Command creates a registry reservation before capacity admission.
The reservation records requestId, rendererCommandDigest, and deadlineAt.
Registry reservation establishes join and conflict identity but is not accepted execution.
A same-ID same-digest request joins or replays the existing inflight or sealed terminal result.
A same-ID different-digest request returns RENDER_REQUEST_CONFLICT.
A same-ID different-deadline request returns RENDER_REQUEST_CONFLICT.
Engine admission uses a bounded FIFO queue.
Active registry lookup precedes queue admission.
Accepted execution linearizes only when a FIFO queue position is atomically acquired.
Failure to acquire a queue position returns nonterminal RENDER_ENGINE_BUSY.
A BUSY reservation remains until the original deadline.
A BUSY request may retry the same digest within the original deadline.
An accepted request's queue wait counts against the deadline and remains cancellable.
Accepted queue wait is bounded to five seconds.
Accepted queue-wait exhaustion returns terminal RENDER_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED and never BUSY.
Ticket19 supplies the exact concurrency-slot, queue-length, and wait bounds.
deadlineAt governs queue, resource, layout, raster, encode, trace, and seal stages.
Engine converts deadlineAt to monotonic remaining time exactly once on ingress.
Exact resend cannot reset or extend the deadline.
Output must atomically seal before the deadline.
Transport of already sealed output may complete after the deadline.
Engine cannot start join or replay after the deadline.
Cancel HTTP entities use application/vnd.renderweave.render-cancel+json with version 1.0.
Authenticated cancel may arrive before Command and create a tombstone retained until the deadline.
Repeated cancel with the same digest is idempotent.
Cancel with a different digest conflicts.
Cancel linearized before atomic output seal returns RENDER_CANCELLED with zero output.
Cancel arriving after seal cannot change success.
HTTP disconnect is not a reliable cancel signal.
Cooperative checkpoints cover queue, every fetch or retry, decode, font parse, layout, every Text shrink iteration, paint chunks, encode chunks, and seal.
A result from an uninterruptible call completed after cancellation is discarded and its slot remains occupied until computation stops.
Ticket19 freezes maximum checkpoint latency and the total deadline.
Lost registry or shard state returns RENDER_REQUEST_STATE_LOST for the same requestId.
Engine never guesses or re-executes after request state loss.
The caller must create a new public render operation and repeat complete Evaluation after state loss.
Public renderOperationId and Engine requestId are distinct and cannot serve as capability keys or replay tokens.
Registry, tombstone, document, lease, temporary image, and trace state is request-isolated in memory or encrypted temporary storage.
Request state is excluded from ordinary logs, dumps, backups, audits, and history.
Unsealed document, lease, resource buffer, raw trace or sidecar, and temporary output are cleaned immediately after terminal or cancel and no later than deadline.
Only minimal terminal registry and an authorized sealed complete response or safe terminal problem may remain until max of sealedAt and deadlineAt plus five minutes for exact replay.
Access, retry, and cancel cannot extend retention.
A pre-Command cancel tombstone is retained for exactly 60 seconds.
Cleanup failure emits only an operational alert and cannot extend public lifecycle.
Engine observable execution follows the specified parse-through-seal stage order.
Unobservable pure preparation may run concurrently only when first error, budgets, resource selection, and output remain equivalent to serial order.
Resources are processed serially in manifest encounter order.
A fetch URL is retried only for transport failure or HTTP 5xx.
Fetch attempts and backoff are Profile-fixed and contain no jitter.
Every fetch attempt rechecks deadline, lease expiry, and cumulative budgets before starting.
HTTP 4xx, expiry, length, hash, media, magic, descriptor, and decode failures receive zero retry.
Ticket19 freezes exact attempt, backoff, byte, and duration limits.
Engine has no cross-request raw or decoded resource cache without a trusted ownerScope partition.
Request-local reuse keys are exactly kind, sha256, byteLength, mediaType, and exact Renderer Profile.
Request-local cache reuse does not bypass occurrence lease, manifest-order, first-error, or budget checks.
Logical current, assetId, resourceId, and URL are not cache keys.
Engine completes encoded bytes, content hash, closed result metadata, and authorized trace before seal.
The registry critical section performs a final cancel and deadline check before seal.
Result and authorized trace seal atomically.
Any pre-seal failure deletes temporary bytes and trace and returns one terminal problem.
After seal, cancel cannot change success and transport truncation can obtain the same result through exact-digest replay.
Engine success and terminal problem are mutually exclusive.
Engine cannot emit partial scene, partial page, placeholder, warning image, best-effort resource, old-image fallback, or success-with-warning output.
Runtime failure creates no business write and cannot delete, restore, replace Asset, or change Template readiness or revision.
Root Canvas trim in points is the rectangle from zero to widthPt and heightPt.
The physical surface expands trim by the four authored bleed values using the specified coordinates.
Output widthPx and heightPx use the specified ROUND_HALF_UP surface-times-DPI formulas.
Surface dimension arithmetic uses exact arbitrary-precision decimal multiplication and division.
Each complete surface width and height is rounded exactly once.
Trim, bleed, and individual edges cannot be rounded before addition.
Zero dimensions, edge, pixel, or encoded-byte overflow, and unsafe allocation fail before resource fetch and surface allocation with a stable output or raster budget code.
Device surface origin is top-left at zero and pixel centers are at half-integer coordinates.
The hard device clip is the half-open rectangle bounded by widthPx and heightPx.
Trim origin uses exact bleed-times-DPI translation and may be subpixel.
Layout, boxes, glyphs, clips, and transforms cannot pixel-snap.
The four surface edges cannot be rounded independently.
Canvas background covers the complete surface including bleed.
PNG preserves Canvas RGBA alpha.
JPEG applies fixed opaque white matte as the final Output Profile operation.
Callers cannot choose JPEG matte.
DPI affects only device lowering and output metadata and cannot feed back into layout, shaping, HUG, line breaking, or Image aspect ratio.
The Renderer Profile output color contract is only SRGB_8BIT.
IMAGE technical descriptors require colorEncoding equal to SRGB_8BIT.
Asset admission accepts only no-profile, standard-sRGB declaration, or the fixed canonical sRGB ICC as equivalent color inputs.
Asset admission rejects conflicting, damaged, arbitrary ICC, CMYK or YCCK, HDR, and wide-gamut inputs.
Engine re-proves the color contract from exact bytes and does not trust descriptor assertions.
Static PNG decode accepts only legal grayscale, indexed, RGB, or RGBA forms with 1, 2, 4, or 8-bit depth and legal tRNS.
PNG decode rejects 16-bit PNG and APNG.
JPEG decode accepts only 8-bit baseline or progressive grayscale or YCbCr.
JPEG decode rejects CMYK or YCCK, 12-bit, and extended formats.
WebP decode accepts only static lossy or lossless content with optional alpha.
WebP decode rejects animation.
Every accepted image is deterministically decoded before orientation is applied.
Every accepted image is converted to straight RGBA8 sRGB before fixed integer premultiplication.
Renderer interprets only color, alpha, and one valid EXIF orientation from image metadata.
Duplicate or conflicting orientation metadata fails.
Orientation is applied exactly once.
Input DPI, time, GPS, thumbnail, software tags, and all other metadata are ignored and not propagated.
Fetch URLs must be canonical HTTPS and reject userinfo, fragments, noncanonical host or port, dot segments, and percent-encoding allowlist bypasses.
Origin and path-prefix authorization matches segment boundaries.
Every connection re-evaluates DNS and egress policy.
Fetch forbids redirect, proxy environment, cookies, range requests, caller headers, and transparent compression.
Renderer Profile fixes request headers.
Fetch accepts only HTTP 200 with identity body and one Content-Length equal to the declared value.
At Command admission every resource expiresAt must cover deadlineAt plus the Renderer Profile safety margin.
Insufficient lease lifetime is treated as an internal handoff violation.
Every fetch attempt rechecks lease expiry.
Bytes fully downloaded before expiry and verified for length, hash, media, magic, and descriptor remain valid within the request after expiry.
Resource leases cannot be renewed by Engine.
The initial FONT subset accepts one-face non-variable monochrome-outline TTF or OTF with the listed outline and shaping tables.
FONT parsing rejects collections, color, bitmap, SVG, Graphite, AAT-only, and malformed or contradictory fonts.
faceIndex zero, flavor, and unitsPerEm must match exact font bytes.
Each Run uses only its exact fontResourceId.
Renderer cannot read system locale or use system, built-in, family, or replacement-glyph fallback.
Missing glyphs in actual text return FONT_GLYPH_MISSING.
Renderer cannot draw notdef as a missing-glyph substitute.
Invalid post or OS/2 decoration metrics return FONT_DECORATION_METRICS_MISSING only when the corresponding underline or strike is actually used.
v1 has no authored locale, language, or OpenType feature switches.
Layout Profile uses fixed Unicode data, inferred script, language und, writingMode, and fixed BiDi, vertical-orientation, line, grapheme, shaping versions, and feature set.
Environment, OS, CPU, and font-discovery order cannot change shaping results.
The authoritative Renderer uses CPU raster only.
GPU, LCD subpixel, dither, hinting, embedded bitmap, autohint, and runtime CPU or SIMD dispatch are forbidden.
Text uses fixed grayscale antialiasing and vectors use fixed antialiasing.
Machine manifest pins Skia, FreeType, compiler, build arguments, and one x86-64-v2 path while exact build and goldens define coverage, edge, and sampling ties.
Every OS, CPU, or SIMD target must independently pass the exact corpus before READY.
Straight RGBA8 converts to premultiplied sRGB8 using the specified ROUND_HALF_UP channel-times-alpha formula.
Premultiplication forces RGB to zero when alpha is zero.
Opacity, coverage, and Porter-Duff source-over use the Profile-fixed 8-bit premultiplied order.
Renderer does not blend in linear-light space.
PNG unpremultiplies by the Profile-fixed rule and keeps fully transparent RGB at zero.
Image sampling occurs after orientation and sRGB normalization.
Device pixel centers remain half-integer during sampling.
NEAREST uses the Profile-fixed nearest-neighbor and tie rule.
LINEAR uses premultiplied-RGBA8 bilinear sampling.
Sampling clamps source edges and forbids transparent extension, mipmaps, and higher-order filters.
CONTAIN bars remain transparent and JPEG matte is applied only immediately before final encoding.
After composing all world transforms, QR and Barcode allow only translation, positive uniform scale, and arbitrary rotation.
Reflection, skew, and nonuniform scale return TRANSFORM_UNSUPPORTED.
The local module grid uses the largest centered integer pitch that fits the final physical box including quiet zone.
Module pitch below one device pixel returns MODULE_TOO_SMALL.
Codes render first as a local integer grid with nearest sampling and then rotate by the fixed nearest rule without feeding back into layout.
QR encodes UTF-8 byte mode and always writes ECI 26.
QR error correction comes from the authored value.
QR selects the smallest fitting version from 1 through 40 and the lowest-penalty mask with smaller mask ID as tie-breaker.
QR quiet zone is exactly four modules.
QR content overflow returns CODE_CONTENT_TOO_LARGE.
EAN-8, EAN-13, and UPC-A require an already-valid check digit and use their specified left and right quiet zones.
Code 128 accepts only printable ASCII.
Code 128 chooses the minimum-codeword B or C plan, breaking ties by earlier switch and then set B.
Code 128 computes the standard checksum and uses a 10X quiet zone on both sides.
Barcodes paint bars across the complete usable height and never render human-readable text.
PNG chunk order is exactly signature, IHDR, sRGB intent zero, pHYs, one or more IDAT, and IEND.
PNG forbids other chunks, empty IDAT chunks, and trailing bytes.
IHDR is exactly RGBA8 color type 6 with method zero and noninterlaced output.
PNG pixels-per-meter uses ROUND_HALF_UP of dpi times 5000 divided by 127.
Every PNG scanline uses filter byte zero.
The sole zlib stream uses header 78 01 and no dictionary.
Uncompressed input is split into stored DEFLATE blocks of at most 65,535 bytes with every nonfinal block full and a nonempty final block.
Only the final DEFLATE block sets BFINAL, padding bits are zero, and LEN and NLEN use complementary little-endian values.
Adler-32 and PNG CRC use their standard algorithms.
The complete zlib stream is split into IDAT payloads of at most 1,048,576 bytes with every nonfinal payload full and a nonempty final payload.
The PNG algorithm plus golden vectors defines renderweave-output-png/1.0 independent of libpng and zlib defaults or versions.
JPEG input is white-matted RGB8 converted to YCbCr and encoded as baseline SOF0, one nonprogressive 4:4:4 nonarithmetic scan.
JPEG quality is the effective Command integer.
The pinned static libjpeg-turbo build disables SIMD and uses JDCT_ISLOW.
JPEG disables optimized Huffman, restart, smoothing, and Adobe APP14 and uses fixed Annex K DC and AC tables.
jpeg_set_defaults and jpeg_set_quality helpers are not contract authority.
The machine manifest stores both 64-entry base quantization tables.
JPEG quantization scaling and entry clamping use the specified integer formulas.
JPEG marker order and all listed JFIF, ICC, table, scan, and entropy fields are exact.
Canonical sRGB ICC uses manifest-pinned full bytes, length, and SHA-256.
Exact libjpeg-turbo source, build, and golden vectors jointly define final entropy bytes.
PNG and JPEG write no time, software, EXIF, XMP, random identifier, or source metadata.
Identical static nodes, exact resources, Profiles, DPI, and JPEG quality produce byte-identical encoded images.
requestId, deadline, lease URL or expiry, retry or cache path, and trace flag cannot change image bytes.
Layout intermediates use Layout Profile tolerances while final pixels are exact and final encoded images are byte-exact.
Any observable pixel change requires a new Renderer Profile.
Encoding-only changes require a new Output Profile, and layout, shaping, or break changes require a new Layout Profile plus a new Renderer compatibility combination when pixels change.
Engine computes contentSha256 only after complete encoding.
contentSha256 is exactly SHA-256 of the final encoded image bytes.
contentSha256 is not Evaluation identity, cache key, authorization value, or business Artifact ID.
Success metadata is a closed renderweave-render-result/1.0 object with exactly the listed common members.
JPEG success metadata requires quality while PNG success metadata forbids quality.
A successful response without trace carries raw image/png or image/jpeg bytes.
A trace-free success carries the specified fixed content and RenderWeave headers.
JPEG success additionally carries RenderWeave-Quality.
Rendering verifies response headers, Command, body length, and digest before public release.
diagnostics.layoutTrace defaults to false.
Only independently authorized Rendering may set layoutTrace true.
Successful trace is a closed renderweave-layout-trace/1.0 value.
Trace projects Canvas, synthetic occurrences, invisible items, and zero-opacity items in RenderDocument preorder.
Each trace item contains only the allowed opaque identity, box, transform, bounds, clip, paint index, and overflow fields.
Diagnostic binary64 values quantize to six decimal places with HALF_EVEN and encode negative zero as zero.
Trace quantization never feeds back into layout or paint.
A trace success response is multipart/related with exactly two ordered parts and no extras.
The first multipart part is the closed result-with-trace JSON media type containing result and layoutTrace.
The second multipart part is the raw image.
Each multipart part carries its own Content-Digest.
Rendering verifies part count, order, media type, requestId, closed JSON, length, and hash before atomic public release.
Trace overflow returns RENDER_LAYOUT_TRACE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with zero image and cannot truncate trace.
A caller may issue a new no-trace request after trace overflow.
Engine returns only opaque trace to Rendering.
Before seal Rendering uses request sidecar and permission projection to remove unauthorized fields rather than emit placeholders.
Rendering atomically seals the final authorized trace projection into the response.
Raw sidecar, unsealed trace, multipart temporary content, and locator mapping are cleaned immediately after terminal or cancel and no later than deadline.
Authorized sealed safe trace and multipart bytes may remain only with the sealed response until the Ticket19 five-minute exact-replay cutoff.
Exact replay cannot depend on raw sidecar re-projection.
TCP or HTTP chunks do not constitute product partial output.
A receiver displays or saves output only after verifying complete length, digest, result, and body.
A truncated response is deleted and recovered only by exact replay of the same Command.
v1 does not automatically persist successful image bytes.
Rendering decides whether an authorized public response is streamed.
Engine terminal failure returns exactly one closed renderweave-render-problem/1.0 object.
A render problem has exactly the listed required and optional members.
Inapplicable optional problem members are omitted rather than null.
Each code uses a closed low-cardinality safe parameters object.
Problem parameters forbid free text, paths, business text, URL, token, hash, raw cause, and stack.
Rendering owns retry classification and Engine returns no boolean retry hint.
Problem HTTP entities use application/vnd.renderweave.render-problem+json with version 1.0.
HTTP status is transport mapping only and clients use stable code for semantics.
engineStage is closed to the eleven listed stage values.
Command and document admission may boundedly collect errors by canonical field order.
After resource processing begins Engine returns strictly the first error.
Post-resource first-error order is manifest order, tree preorder, property declaration order, then Run index.
Control failures use the listed stable RENDER control codes.
Resource failures reuse the listed resource codes and add FONT_DECORATION_METRICS_MISSING and RESOURCE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED.
Layout and output failures use at least the listed stable layout, code, raster, output, and trace codes.
Capacity problem parameters expose only oracle-defined limitId and never actual count or input value.
Malformed sealed document and digest, manifest, descriptor, Profile, encoder, or seal invariant violations use detailed internal codes and redacted operational alerts.
Public Rendering folds internal invariant failures to RENDER_INTERNAL_ERROR.
Legal-but-unrenderable failures retain their specific public code.
HTTP status maps success, malformed Command, conflict or cancel, unrenderable, upstream resource, busy, deadline, and internal categories to the specified statuses.
HTTP status mapping never changes code semantics.
Rendering resends the same Command only for RENDER_ENGINE_BUSY or unknown transport outcome.
Rendering does not retry timeout, cancel, 4xx, expiry, integrity, decode, layout, raster, or encode failures.
Engine alone performs permitted internal resource 5xx retry.
Legal overflow, signed overlap, low contrast, and one-to-three-pixel module outcomes do not create warnings.
Authorized trace may expose only fixed flags for such legal outcomes.
There is no warning array, automatic repair, or success-with-error state.
renderweave-renderer/1.0 is jointly defined by machine-readable algorithm, dependency, and feature manifest, a fixed reference implementation commit, and golden corpus.
Prose explains boundaries but cannot replace executable conformance vectors.
Raster manifest pins Skia, FreeType, compiler, build hash, and one CPU path.
JPEG manifest pins libjpeg-turbo source and build plus quantization, Huffman, and ICC bytes.
The self-described PNG algorithm still requires boundary golden verification.
Engine startup reads a read-only certified manifest and enters READY only when the complete exact compatibility combination is supported and evidenced on the current platform.
Internal health or capability may be exposed internally but is neither visible nor selectable by public callers.
Layout, shaping, and break changes publish a new Layout Profile.
Decoder, orientation, color, font parser, raster, antialias, sampling, and QR or Barcode changes publish a new Renderer Profile.
Encoded-bitstream or metadata-only changes with unchanged pixels publish a new Output Profile.
Wire changes publish a new corresponding contract version.
Changes to accepted Asset feature scope publish a new AssetAcceptanceProfile.
Engine build version, library patch, or environment default cannot silently hot-fix old Profile semantics.
Ticket19 supplies exact values for Renderer Profile semantic per-request limits.
A deployment is READY only if it can honor every Profile limit without silently lowering memory or CPU ceilings.
Deployment concurrency and queue capacity may return BUSY before accepted execution.
An accepted request must complete within contract budgets or return a contract error.
READY evidence covers strict wire, canonicalization, digest, layout, shaping, exact pixels, and exact PNG and JPEG bytes.
READY evidence covers QR and Barcode matrices, image decode, malformed IMAGE and FONT, descriptors, and fetch-security faults.
READY evidence covers deadline, cancel, retry, registry or shard loss, and output or multipart verification.
Every allowed OS, CPU, and SIMD combination independently replays the evidence corpus.
Screenshots, one-sided unit tests, old Haibo tests, and claims based on Skia defaults cannot certify READY.

The old busbox renderer may contribute implementation and test foundations but its listed wire, DPI, concurrency, font, control, descriptor, trace, locator, and environmental semantics are incompatible.
A successor implementation must provide new parsers, profiles, resource paths, and control paths and pass the new corpus.
An adapter or version-string change cannot claim equivalence to this contract.
The historical Haibo Render Artifact and browser-SVG preview cannot prove this image Renderer or Output Profile contract.
Ticket19 must freeze exact maximum DPI and surface edge, pixel, decoded-byte, and encoded-byte limits.
Ticket19 must freeze exact queue, slot, deadline, and checkpoint limits.
Ticket19 must freeze resource attempt, backoff, fetch-byte, and total-duration limits.
Ticket19 must freeze manifest and request-local cache limits.
Ticket19 must freeze font-table, glyph, shaping, paint, and clip limits.
Ticket19 must freeze QR and Barcode module and content limits.
Ticket19 must freeze PNG and JPEG encoding limits.
Ticket19 must freeze trace item, trace byte, and multipart limits.
Ticket19 must freeze registry and temporary-state retention limits.
Ticket19 must support frozen limits with peak-memory, CPU, and fault-injection evidence.
v1 excludes multi-output, batch, page, and node export.
v1 excludes crop, resize, target-size, and background override.
v1 excludes WebP, SVG, PDF, and HTML output.
v1 excludes GPU rendering.
v1 excludes cross-request output and resource caches.
v1 excludes Artifact, Workspace, and history persistence.
v1 excludes public RenderDSL, Command, and Engine APIs.
v1 excludes partial output, warning image, and placeholder output.
v1 excludes default and replacement fonts.
v1 excludes arbitrary ICC, HDR, and CMYK.
v1 excludes variable, color, and bitmap fonts.
v1 excludes caller Profile selection, old Haibo fallback, and environment defaults.
v1 excludes lease renewal and replacement of URLs or Asset current.
v1 excludes continuing after partial failure and Engine-triggered re-Evaluation.
Ticket16 freezes exploration specification, domain language, and later implementation and acceptance constraints only.
Ticket16 creates no Renderer, client, API, queue, registry, cache, codec, Artifact, table, route, deployment configuration, or placeholder implementation.
